blocks.text:
OCEAN AS BIOSPHERE
==================

  SUNLIT ZONE (0-200 m)            ← PRIMARY PRODUCTION ENGINE
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Phytoplankton: ~50% of Earth's O₂ production            │
  │  Zooplankton, fish larvae, marine mammals, seabirds       │
  │  Coral reefs: 0.1% of ocean floor, ~25% of species       │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
               │ Biological Pump (sinking particles)
               ▼
  TWILIGHT ZONE (200-1000 m)        ← ACTIVE MIGRATION LAYER
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Diel vertical migrants: feed at surface at night         │
  │  Lanternfishes, krill, squid, siphonophores               │
  │  Largest daily animal migration on Earth (by biomass)     │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
               │
               ▼
  MIDNIGHT ZONE (1000-4000 m)       ← PERMANENT DARKNESS
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  No light. Pressure: 100-400 atm                          │
  │  Bioluminescence: dominant signaling modality             │
  │  Marine snow (detritus) as primary food source            │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
               │
               ▼
  ABYSSAL ZONE (4000-6000 m)        ← VAST DEEP PLAINS
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Covers ~60% of Earth's surface — least studied           │
  │  Abyssal plains: soft sediment, polymetallic nodules      │
  │  Pressure: 400-600 atm. Temperature: 0-3°C               │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
               │
               ▼
  HADAL ZONE (>6000 m)              ← TRENCH ECOSYSTEMS
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Ocean trenches: subduction zones. 37 total worldwide     │
  │  Mariana Trench: 10,935 m (Challenger Deep)               │
  │  Amphipods, holothurians, bacteria under extreme pressure  │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  CHEMOSYNTHETIC ECOSYSTEMS         ← SUNLIGHT-INDEPENDENT LIFE
  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Hydrothermal vents: H₂S oxidation → primary production  │
  │  Cold seeps: methane as energy source                     │
  │  Whale falls: ~30-year succession community               │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

MARINE BIOLOGY
├── Biological Oceanography   — organisms + physical ocean interaction
├── Marine Ecology            — community structure, food webs, trophic dynamics
├── Marine Physiology         — pressure/cold/salt adaptation mechanisms
├── Systematic Ichthyology    — fish taxonomy and evolution
├── Cetology                  — whales, dolphins, porpoises
├── Marine Microbiology       — bacteria, archaea, viruses in ocean
│   ├── Biological pump       — carbon export to deep ocean
│   └── Microbial loop        — dissolved organic carbon cycling
├── Deep-Sea Biology          — hadal and abyssal life
│   ├── Hydrothermal biology  — vent chemosynthetic communities
│   └── Cold seep biology     — methane seep communities
├── Marine Conservation       — MPAs, fisheries, climate impacts
└── Coral Reef Ecology        — reef ecosystems, bleaching, structure

          ▼                   ▼                    ▼
   OCEANOGRAPHY         EVOLUTIONARY          CLIMATE SCIENCE
   Physical/chemical    BIOLOGY               Ocean as CO₂ sink
   ocean properties:    Cetacean return-      Biological pump
   temperature,         to-sea,               Acidification,
   salinity, currents,  convergent            species range
   pressure             evolution,            shifts
                        island biogeography
          │                   │
          ▼                   ▼
   ECOLOGY               ASTROBIOLOGY
   Trophic dynamics,     Chemosynthetic
   keystone species,     ecosystems as
   community succession, models for
   MPAs                  Europa/Enceladus

DEPTH vs PHYSICAL CONDITIONS
═════════════════════════════

Depth (m)   Pressure    Light          Temperature     O₂
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
0           1 atm       Full sunlight  0-30°C surface  High
200         20 atm      ~1% surface    Thermocline      Moderate
600         60 atm      0.001%         4-8°C            OMZ minimum
1,000       100 atm     None           4°C              OMZ low
4,000       400 atm     None           2°C              Moderate
6,000       600 atm     None           1-2°C            Low
10,935      ~1,100 atm  None           1-2°C            Low

OMZ = Oxygen Minimum Zone (~200-1000 m). O₂ depleted by bacterial
decomposition of sinking organic matter. Fish and invertebrates
avoid this layer; some adapted to exploit it.

blocks.heading_context: ## Primary Production: Where Energy Enters the Ocean
blocks.text:
PHOTOSYNTHETIC vs CHEMOSYNTHETIC PRIMARY PRODUCTION
════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SUNLIT OCEAN (>99% of total marine primary production)
  6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
  Producers: diatoms, dinoflagellates, coccolithophores, cyanobacteria
  Global rate: ~50 Pg C/year
  Key constraints: NITROGEN and IRON (not CO₂ or light in open ocean)

CHEMOSYNTHETIC ECOSYSTEMS (<1% of total, locally significant)
  H₂S + CO₂ + O₂ → CH₂O + H₂SO₄    (sulfur-oxidizing bacteria)
  CH₄ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O              (methanotrophs at cold seeps)
  Producers: Gammaproteobacteria, ANME archaea
  Key constraint: flux of H₂S or CH₄ from geological sources
  Significance: life without sunlight — primary model for life elsewhere
